PART IV (A) — PROVINCIAL COUNCIL
Provincial Council Notification
Livestock Statute No. 03 of 2017 of the Provincial Council of the North Western Province

A statute to Provide for the Implementation of Provincial Livestock Policies towards a Sustainable Development in the North Western Province; For the Realization of objectives ; To Provide for the Formulation, Implementation and Operation of Plans with Regard to the Preserva-tion, Taking care and Development of Livestock and Prevention of animal Diseases and for Matters connected therewith and Incidental thereto and to provide for the repeal of North Western Provincial animal husbandry statute No. 04 of 1998. This Statute shall be inconsistent as applicable with the Animal Act, No. 29 of 1958 as amended by the Act, No. 10 of 1968, the Act, No. 46 of 1988 and the Act, No. 10 of 2009; the Animal Feed Act, No. 15 of 1986; the Butchers Ordinance No. 9 of 1893 as amended by the Butchers

(Amendment) Act, No.44 of 1947, the Butchers (Amendment) Act, No.02 of 1951, the Butchers (Amendment) Act, No.48 of 1953, the Butchers (Amendment) Act, No.31 of 1976 and the Butchers (Amendment) Act, No.60 of 1981; the Epidemic Act, No. 33 of 1952; and the Anti Rabies Act, No. 23 of 1956. Be it enacted by the Provincial Council of the North Western Province of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka as follows :
01. This Statute may be cited as the Livestock Statute, No.03 of 2017 of the Provincial Council of
the North Western Province.
02. This Statute shall come into operation on such date as may be appointed by the Governor of the
North Western Province. 03. Objectives of the Statute are as follows: (1) To provide for the formulation, planning, implementation, operation and regulation of
policies relating to livestock in compliance with the national policies and needs of the province; (2) To provide legal provisions for the preservation, regulation, caring, improving of

livestock and production and use of animal feed and medicines and prevention of animal diseases within the North Western Province; (3) To establish the North Western Provincial Department of Animal Production and Health; (4) To establish the North Western Provincial Livestock Development Committee; (5) To empower farmers engaged in the livestock sector in the North Western Province; (6) To establish Zonal and Regional Livestock Development Committees and Rural
Livestock Development Societies of those engaged in the livestock sector in the North Western Province; (7) To ensure the maintenance of environment friendly farms of prescribed standard and
healthy and qualitative animal production in the province; (8) To establish and manage the North Western Provincial Dairy Promotion Fund.
Part I Policy Planning, Management and Regulation 04. The Provincial Ministry in charge of the subject shall be vested with the policy planning on

animal production, health and development in the North Western Province in compliance with the national policy and needs of the province. For the purpose, proposals from the rural, regional, zonal and provincial livestock development committees established within the province and those of the government, semi-government, co-operative, non-government, volunteer organizations and volunteers may be sought. 05. The Provincial Director shall prepare a five year Provincial Livestock Development Plan

giving due consideration to the proposals of the institutions, organizations or persons referred to at section 04 above and submit same for the approval of the Provincial Livestock Development Committee once in every 05 years.

06. The Provincial Ministry and the Department in charge of the subject shall provide livestock

and health, breeding, extension, training, marketing, promotion and provincial research services needed by those engaged in livestock sector within the province. 07. The Animal Development Advisory Divisions and zones shall be determined on the basis of the

National policy and extension of the population, extent of land, animal population, climatic conditions and administrative boundaries within the province and Regional Veterinary Medical Officer’s Division shall be determined on the basis of administrative boundaries. 08. Provincial Research Institutions may be established and maintained for the needs of the live-
stock development field within the province.
09. Human resources development Divisions or Units may be established for the purpose of em-
powering stakeholders with a view to promoting livestock development.
Part II Establishment, composition, powers and functions of the Provincial Depart-
ment of Animal Production and Health
10. There shall be established a Department which shall be called “North Western Provincial

Department of Animal Production and Health” (herein after referred to as the “Department”) to implement the provisions and to achieve objectives of this Statute. 11. The North Western Provincial Department of Animal Production and Health shall, by the

name assigned to it be a body corporate and shall have a perpetual succession and a common seal and may carry out all functions related to the livestock sector and sue and be sued in such name and may make submissions with regard to other legal affairs. 12. The First Class Veterinary Medical officer who called as the Director of Animal Production

and Health Service shall be appointed by the Governor of the North Western Province asking the Minister of the subject to implement the statutes wested by the Department according to the relevant Service Minute. 13. For the purpose of execution of the duties and functions of the Department, there may be

appointed Additional Provincial Directors, Subject Specialists, Deputy Directors, District Veterinary Medical officers, Veterinary Medical officers, Animal Husbandry Officers, Animal Development Instructors, and other ancillary staff. 14. All officers and employees who are in service of the North Western Provincial Department

of Animal Production and Health on the day of coming into operation of this Statute shall be deemed to have appointed under this Statute. 15. (1) Powers to execute the directions and orders made for the purpose of provisions of this

Statue and matters incidental thereto shall be vested in the Director subject to the general administration of the Secretary. (2) The Director may exercise the powers vested in him by delegating such powers to
other officers of the Department as the case may be. (3) The Director shall account to the Secretary for the management of all physical,
financial and human resources including moveable and immovable assets of the Department.

16. (1) The Provincial Director or any other officer duly authorized by the Provincial Director

shall have the powers to enter and inspect any farm or manufacturing plant or sales outlet or cold storage at any time for the purpose of execution of provisions under this Statute. (2) No person shall obstruct any authorized officer exercising his powers under this Statute
or regulations made there under. (3) The owner or the person in charge of or every person present at the site subjected to

inspection shall be bound to provide the officer carrying out the inspection under subsection (1) of section 16 above with samples or other information as required by the officer in carrying out his duties. (4) No person shall provide false or misleading samples or information to any officer
engaged in obtaining samples or information in a formal manner. 17. The Department shall execute following functions for the development, preservation,

promotion, extension and regularization of livestock within the province: (1) to formulate and implement the annual plan in compliance with five year Plan; (2) to ensure health care of animal by control, prevention of and treatment to animal
diseases; (3) to carry out breeding for the maintenance of an environmental friendly animal

population of high genetic quality which suits the needs of the province; (4) to implement extension and training programmes; (5) to implement production and sales promotional programmes; (6) to conduct provincial researches and surveys and publicize their results; (7) to introduce new technology and farm mechanizations which suit the province; (8) to liaise with research institutes of national, provincial and regional level, universities
and other institutes related to animal husbandry; (9) to introduce, distribute and sell high quality breeding and plant materials necessary for
the development of animal farming; (10) to register, issue licenses to, supervise and regulate all institutions, organizations and

persons related to the field of livestock : I. rural societies and regional and zonal livestock development committees ; II. animal farms ; III. animal feed, animal breeding matters, livestock medicine, chemicals,
equipment and manufacturing plants or manufacturers; IV. animal feed, animal breeding matters, livestock medicine, chemicals or

equipment distribution institutions or distributors or sales outlets ; V. all livestock product cold stores within the province; VI. institutions which purchase livestock manufactured within the province ;

institutions and promotion of animal husbandry within the province, shall be prepared by the Director and be submitted for approval of the Secretary before 31st date of October of the current year, based on the Provincial livestock development plan prepared in terms of the provisions of section 05 of this statute. (2) The annual performance report relevant to each calender year shall be prepared by the
Director and be submitted to the Secretary prior to 15th date of March of next year.
Part III Registration of Institutions and individuals 19. All organizations and persons below mentioned who are engaged in livestock sector in the

North Western Province, shall obtain a Certificate of Registration issued by the Director and the same shall be renewed annually. (1) rural societies and regional and zonal livestock development committee. (2) animal farms.

For the purpose of registration under section 19 above, the applicant shall: (1) make the application on the specimen prescribed by the Provincial Director. (2) pay a registration fee as prescribed by the Minister. (3) comply with the criteria and standards specified by regulations made under Section 84 (1) of this Statute. (4) fulfill all other legal requirements as required by other institutions in addition to the regulations of this Statute. 21. No person shall transfer or alienate the certificate of registration or alter any information contained therein without the approval of the Provincial Director. 22. If any application for registration made under Section 19 shall not be entertained unless it meets the requirements specified in Section 20, the same shall not be registered and be in formed thereof to the applicant in writing. 23. (1) When the Director determines that any institution, individual or organization that has been registered under Section 19 of this Statute, acts in contravention of the objectives of the Statute or does not comply with the standards specified by regulations, the registration of such institution, individual or organization may be temporarily suspended. (2) In the event of temporarily suspension of registration, the Director shall inform in writing the reasons lead to such suspension to the holder of the certificate of registration. (3) When the registration is temporarily suspended, if the institution, individual or organization whose registration is so suspended takes actions to make good the reasons lead to such suspension and to meet the stipulated requirements within a reasonable time as determined by the Director, the registration of such institution, individual or volunteer organization shall be reinstated. 24. If the requirements within the stipulated reasonable time as per section 23 (3) of this Statute are failed to be met, the registration shall be cancelled and be informed thereof to the applicant concerned. 25. an appeal there from to the Minister in charge of the subject within 45 days from the receipt of such notice. 26. (1) When an appeal is received under Section 25 of this Statute, the Minister shall direct the

Secretary to conduct an inquiry and determine thereon. (2)The Secretary after conducting an inquiry, shall make recommendations to the Minister to confirm or revise or reject the determination of the Director. (3) The Minister shall submit his decision within 45 days from the receipt of the appeal and the decision of the Minister thereon shall be final and conclusive. 27. (1) When a person who has been convicted by Court under section 92 of this Statute for the

offence of maintaining a farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or sales outlet without a license issued under section 19 of this Statute or regulations made thereunder, continues to maintain the farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or sales outlet, an order may be issued on a request made in that regard from the Magistrate's Court by the Director or any other person authorized by him, directing such person to close down such farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or sales outlet until such time the person concerned ob tains a license again. (2) In any proceeding under the above section, the certificate issued by the Director or any other officer duly authorized by him shall be prima facie evidence of the content therein to the effect that the person whose name appears on the certificate continues to maintain the farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or the sales outlet without a license. (3) Provided however that, in the event of submission of an appeal under Section 25 of this Statute, the closure shall be deferred pending the determination of the appellate inquiry. (4) When the decision of the Director is confirmed under Section 23 (2) of this Statute and at the appellate inquiry, action shall be taken to close down within 30 days from the date of the appellate determination. 28. When the Provincial Director identifies any premises as a threat to the maintenance of animal
welfare of the province, he shall obtain a temporary closing order in that regard from a Magistrate court. 29. (1) When any person fails to comply with the closing order issued under Section 27(1) of

this Statute, the Magistrate shall issue an order requiring and authorizing the fiscal of the court to close down the farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or sales outlet mentioned in the said order and the fiscal shall execute such order on a date prior to not later than three full days or sooner than seven full days from the date of the order. (2) The order shall be sufficient authority for the fiscal or any other police officer authorized by him for the purpose to enter the farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or sales outlet together with the assistants deemed necessary for the purpose of closing down such farm, cold storage, manufacturing plant or sales outlet.

implementation of the Livestock Statute of the Province. The Provincial Minister in charge of the subject of Livestock shall be the Chairman of the Committee and the Secretary to the Provincial Ministry in charge of the subject of the Livestock shall be the Secretary to the

33. The term of office of the members appointed by the Minister shall be two years.
34. Where a member appointed by the Minister vacates office by expiry of term of office,

resignation, removal by the Minister at his discretion, absence from three consecutive meetings, death or insanity, the Minister shall fill the vacancy so created. 35. The Provincial Committee shall meet at least once in every two months. The Secretary, if

found necessary, may convene supplementary meetings of the Committee on the direction of the Chairman. 36. (1) The quorum of the Committee shall be ⅓ of the membership. (2) The existence of vacancies in the Committee shall not hinder the conduct of meetings of the Committee or the making of decisions at such meetings. 37. The powers and functions of the Provincial Livestock Development Committee shall be :- (1) to submit recommendations and proposals for the formulation of policies pertaining to matters stipulated in this Statute in compliance with the National Policy and needs of the province; (2) to provide necessary advice for the operation and implementation of matters stipulated in the Statute; (3) to approve the five year Livestock Development Plan and other long term and medium term development plans forwarded to the Committee; (4) to take follow up actions and to review the formulation and implementation of the Provincial Livestock Development Policy while providing necessary resources, guidance and assistance for the same; (5) to grant prior approval for any programme or project for the extension and promotion of and education on livestock, provision of services and for researches on livestock to be implemented within the province by any governmental or non-governmental institution, organization, foundation, society, project, programme or similar institution, individual or group of persons and to take appropriate action when relevant conditions are violated. (6) to resolve the issues submitted to the Provincial Livestock Committee. 38. (1) The Provincial Committee may make procedures for the conduct of business of the

meetings of the Committee. (2) The members of the Committee participating in the meetings thereof may be remunerated at such rates as may be determined by the Minister and be approved by the Governor.
Part V
Rural Livestock Development Societies 39. The farmers engaged in livestock activities in a Grama Niladhari division or any part thereof

or several divisions may get together and set up Rural Livestock Development Societies for each field of animal husbandry or in amalgamation and every such society shall be registered with the Department.

40. Rural Livestock Development Society shall, by the name assigned to it be a body corpo-

rate and shall have perpetual succession and a common seal and may carry out all functions related to the livestock sector and may sue and be sued in such name. 41. The object of setting up of these societies shall be to develop the livestock sector by

mobilizing those who are engaged in the livestock sector at rural level and thereby empow-ering them. 42. Qualifications to be eligible for membership: (1) to be a citizen of Sri Lanka; (2) to be not less than 18 years of age; (3) the farm to be located within the area of authority of the Livestock Development Society; (4) the farm to have registered with the Department of Animal Productions. 43. Every Rural Livestock Development Society shall appoint an executive committee

comprising of Chairman, Secretary, Treasurer, Vice-chairman, Co-Secretary and six members and the term of office of such office bearers shall be one year from the appointment. 44.(1) The Director shall prepare the constitution for the Rural Livestock Development

Societies which shall be approved by the Minister. (2) Every Rural Livestock Development Society shall comply with the constitution. 45. The powers and functions of Rural Livestock Development Societies: (1) to formulate and implement livestock development plan for the area of authority of the society, in compliance with the provincial plan and co-ordinate and regulate the implementation of the said plan; (2) to facilitate and liaise with relevant institutions for the development of farms of members; (3) to resolve issues relating to livestock sector arising within the area of authority of the society; (4) to maintain an updated data base relevant to the sector and disseminate such data to relevant parties when the need arises; (5) to implement loan schemes for members of the society; (6) to implement programmes to enhance the funds of the society; (7) to work for the welfare of members of the society; (8) to nominate a member to represent the Regional Livestock development Committee; (9) to implement the insurance scheme; (10) to organize programmes to create new farmers. 46. (1) Meetings of the Society shall be convened once in every month or two months and
supplementary meetings of the Society may be convened at the request of the majority of members.

(1) When a member vacates office by reason of : I. resignation; II. absence from three consecutive meetings; III. death or insanity; IV. removal at the will of the majority members on grounds of any breach of the Constitution or distancing from the livestock sector; such member shall cease to be a member. There shall be paid into the Rural Livestock Development Fund: I. the membership subscription; II. donations by the State, Provincial, Non-Governmental organizations; III. donations by individuals; IV. interest and dividends of the fund; V. All money received from other sources. 49. The Accounts of the Fund : (1) The accounts of the Fund of the society shall be maintained in a State Bank and the accounts of fund shall be maintained as provided by the Constitution of the society. (2) The Director or any other officer authorized by him shall examine the accounts of the Fund annually or as appropriate. 50. (1) The supervision of the affairs of, examination of books of and providing guidance and advice to Rural Livestock Development Societies established within his area of authority shall be vested in the Animal Development Advisor. (2) Any officer duly authorized by the director for the purpose, may supervise and examine the books of Rural Livestock Development Societies. 51. (1) The Director shall appoint a staff grade public officer as the liquidator to cancel the

registration and to liquidate any registered Rural Livestock Development Society on any one or more of the following grounds: (I) the membership declines to less than eleven; (II) being defunct for a period exceeding one year; (III) has acted contrary to its objects; (IV) a number of members not less than two thirds (⅔) of the membership making a re quest to the Director citing that the society has failed to act for the achievement of its objectives. (2) The liquidator appointed under Subsection 51(1) above shall have the following

Part IX
General 84. (1) The Minister shall issue necessary instructions, guidance and orders for the
implementation of provisions of the Statute. (2) The Minister shall demarcate the divisions referred to in Section 7 of this Statute and
such demarcations shall be published in the Gazette. (3) The Minister shall have the power to impose restrictions as appropriate in transporting
animals within and out of the province. (4) The Minister shall have the power to make regulations in respect of prevention and
control of animal diseases within the province. 85. (1) Every regulation made by the Minister under this Statute shall be published in the Gazette

and shall come into operation on the date of such publication or on such date as may be specified in such regulation. (2) Every regulation made by the Minister shall, as soon as it is convenient after its

publication in the Gazette, be brought before the Provincial Council for approval. Any regulation which is not so approved by the Provincial Council, shall be deemed to be rescinded as from the date of disapproval but without prejudices to anything previously made thereunder and a notification to the effect shall be published in the Gazette. 86. (1) Any person aggrieved by any provision of this Statute or any regulation made under this
Statute or by any order or decision made by any officer, may prefer an appeal to the Minister.

Part X
Offences and Penalties 92. Every person, establishment or organization who contravenes any provisions of this Statute or
any regulation made thereunder shall be guilty of an offence under this Statute. 93. Every person who contravenes or fails to comply with any provision of this Statute, shall on

conviction after summary trial by a Magistrate be punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or to a fine not exceeding rupees hundred thousand or to both such fine and imprisonment. 94. (1) Where an offence under this Statute is committed, the Provincial Director or any other
officer authorized by him shall have the power to institute action. (2) The Provincial Director or the officer authorized by him shall take action to recover the
fines charged by the Courts under Section 92 of this Statute, to the Dairy Promotion Fund.
